method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of the ASHM candidiasis page. Doses, concentrations and durations compared character by character. RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-22: the page in retrieved_from was fetched again and every claim attributed to this source was re-checked against it. Quotes stored from the earlier scrape carried that scrape's table and list markup (pipes, numbered list markers) into the quoted string; each was replaced with the text the page actually carries, located by alignment against the retrieved copy (scripts/repair_quotes.py). No dose, duration or concentration changed: the set of numbers in every repaired quote was compared before and after, and the only difference across 156 repaired quotes was list numerals 1-4 becoming bullets. Where a reference superscript falls inside a quoted sentence the page renders it inline, so it appears in source_text; it is part of the retrieved text, not part of the assertion.

claims.claim: Candida species can be normal flora and therefore do not need treatment if asymptomatic
claims.source_text: Candida species can be normal flora and therefore not need treatment if asymptomatic.

claims.claim: Candidiasis can be sexually transmitted but is not considered a sexually transmissible infection
claims.source_text: Can be sexually transmitted but is not considered a sexually transmitted infection (STI).

claims.claim: Candidiasis can arise spontaneously or secondary to disturbance of vaginal flora such as antibiotic therapy, or increased oestrogen levels such as pregnancy or postmenopausal oestrogen therapy
claims.source_text: Can arise spontaneously or secondary to disturbance of vaginal flora e.g. antibiotic therapy or increased oestrogen levels e.g. pregnancy, postmenopausal oestrogen therapy.

claims.claim: Candida glabrata is treated with boric acid 600 mg vaginal pessaries from a compounding pharmacy, one nocte for 14 days, and boric acid can be fatal if ingested and must be avoided in pregnancy
claims.source_text: Candida glabrata Boric acid 600 mg vaginal pessaries (from a compounding pharmacy), one nocte for 14 days (boric acid can be fatal if ingested, avoid in pregnancy

claims.claim: The alternative for Candida glabrata is 100 000 IU nystatin inserted per vaginally for 14 days
claims.source_text: 100 000 IU nystatin inserted per vaginally for 14 days

claims.claim: Uncomplicated candidiasis is treated with vaginal azole creams such as clotrimazole 10% vaginal cream, 1 applicator intravaginally at night as a stat dose or 3-7 day course, or a 500 mg clotrimazole vaginal pessary stat
claims.source_text: Uncomplicated Vaginal azole creams (e.g. clotrimazole 10% vaginal cream, 1 applicator intravaginally at night, as stat. dose or 3-7 day course) or 500 mg clotrimazole vaginal pessary stat

claims.claim: Balanitis is treated with clotrimazole 1% twice daily until symptoms settle then for a further week
claims.source_text: For balanitis, treat with Clotrimazole 1% twice daily until symptoms settle then for a further week.

claims.claim: The alternative for uncomplicated candidiasis is fluconazole 150 mg PO stat
claims.source_text: Fluconazole 150 mg PO, stat.

claims.claim: Recurrent Candida albicans is treated with a longer course of azole cream rather than a stat dose, and/or induction with fluconazole 150 mg PO for 3 doses 3 days apart followed by maintenance fluconazole 150 mg PO weekly for 6 months
claims.source_text: Recurrent Candida albicans Treat each episode with longer course of azole cream (rather than stat. dose) and/or induction with fluconazole 150 mg PO, for 3 doses, 3 days apart, followed by maintenance with fluconazole 150 mg PO, weekly for 6 months

claims.claim: The alternative for recurrent Candida albicans is clotrimazole 10% vaginal cream one applicator nightly for 10-14 days then a 500 mg vaginal pessary weekly after induction
claims.source_text: Clotrimazole 10% vaginal cream (I applicator) nightly for 10-14 days then 500mg vaginal pessary weekly after induction.

claims.claim: Non-albicans species should be considered in cases of confirmed recurrent candidiasis
claims.source_text: Consider non- albicans species in cases of confirmed recurrent candidiasis

claims.claim: Candidiasis is usually diagnosed on the basis of symptoms and signs, with tests useful in recurrent disease
claims.source_text: Usually diagnosed on basis of symptoms and signs. The following tests may be useful in recurrent disease.

claims.claim: High vaginal or self-collected vaginal swab for microscopy and culture enables species differentiation and sensitivities and differentiation from bacterial vaginosis or trichomoniasis
claims.source_text: High vaginal swab or self-collected vaginal swab Microscopy and culture (MCS) Culture for yeast enables species differentiation and sensitivities and differentiation from bacterial vaginosis or trichomoniasis

claims.claim: Recurrent candidiasis is defined as 4 or more episodes in a 12-month period, may occur in nearly 10% of women, and should be confirmed by culture on at least one occasion
claims.source_text: Recurrent candidiasis is defined as 4 or more episodes in a 12-month period and may occur in nearly 10% of women. It should be confirmed by culture on at least one occasion.

claims.claim: Recurrent candidiasis should be confirmed with a vaginal swab for microscopy and culture with speciation
claims.source_text: Recurrent candidiasis should be confirmed with vaginal swab for microscopy and culture with speciation

claims.claim: The auditable outcome is that 100% of patients with recurrent Candida have had yeast cultures and genital examination performed to inform further treatment
claims.source_text: 100% of patients with recurrent C andida have had yeast cultures and genital examination performed to inform further treatment

claims.claim: PCR testing for herpes should be considered only if there are suggestive clinical signs and symptoms
claims.source_text: Consider PCR testing for herpes only if there are suggestive clinical signs and symptoms.

claims.claim: Other causes for symptoms must be excluded by genital examination, such as dermatitis, lichen sclerosis and herpes simplex viruses
claims.source_text: Other causes for symptoms must be excluded by genital examination e.g. dermatitis, lichen sclerosis, herpes simplex viruses (HSVs).

claims.claim: Consider diabetes mellitus, HIV infection or other causes of immunosuppression if disease is poorly controlled
claims.source_text: Consider diabetes mellitus, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection or other causes of immunosuppression if poorly controlled disease.

claims.claim: Reconsider the diagnosis if there is no response to therapy
claims.source_text: Reconsider diagnosis if no response to therapy.

claims.claim: Intravaginal and oral azoles have similar efficacy, topical therapy provides quicker symptom relief, but women generally prefer oral therapy
claims.source_text: Intravaginal and oral azoles have similar efficacy - topical therapy provides quicker symptom relief but women generally prefer oral therapy.

claims.claim: Vulvar treatment alone is inadequate due to a vaginal reservoir and both sites should be treated
claims.source_text: Vulvar treatment alone is inadequate due to a vaginal reservoir - both sites should be treated.

claims.claim: The addition of hydrocortisone 1% cream may provide symptomatic relief
claims.source_text: The addition of hydrocortisone 1% cream may provide symptomatic relief.

claims.claim: There is no evidence that specific diets or use of probiotics influence recurrence
claims.source_text: No evidence that specific diets or use of probiotics influence recurrence.

claims.claim: Oral azoles cannot be used in pregnancy
claims.source_text: Oral azoles cannot be used in pregnancy.

claims.claim: No hepatic monitoring is required for fluconazole use at the doses given
claims.source_text: No hepatic monitoring is required for fluconazole use at the above doses.

claims.claim: More severe disease and symptoms may need longer courses of oral or topical treatment
claims.source_text: More severe disease and symptoms may need longer courses of oral or topical treatment.

claims.claim: Seek specialist advice before treating complicated presentations or recurrent disease that is not responding to therapy
claims.source_text: Consider seeking specialist advice before treating complicated presentations or recurrent disease that is not responding to therapy.

claims.claim: Avoid local irritants such as soap, bath oil, body wash, bubble bath, spermicide, vaginal lubricant and vaginal hygiene products
claims.source_text: Avoid local irritants e.g. soap, bath oil, body wash, bubble bath, spermicide, vaginal lubricant and vaginal hygiene products.

claims.claim: Latex barrier contraception such as condoms can be damaged by antifungal vaginal creams or oil-based products
claims.source_text: Latex barrier contraception e.g. condoms can be damaged by antifungal vaginal creams or oil-based products.

claims.claim: Partners do not usually require treatment
claims.source_text: Partners do not usually require treatment.

claims.claim: Post-coital penile hypersensitivity to vaginal Candida colonisation is possible and responds to partner treatment, and hydrocortisone 1% cream may provide symptomatic relief
claims.source_text: Post-coital penile hypersensitivity to vaginal Candida colonisation is possible and responds to partner treatment Hydrocortisone 1% cream may provide symptomatic relief.

claims.claim: Contact tracing is not required
claims.source_text: Contact tracing is not required.

claims.claim: Penile candidiasis presents as a red rash on the genitals especially under the foreskin, which may or may not be itchy, with swelling of the foreskin if severe, fissures and superficial erosions
claims.source_text: Red rash on genitals, especially under foreskin, may or may not be itchy - Swelling of foreskin if severe - Fissures - Superficial erosions

claims.claim: Vulvovaginal candidiasis presents with thick white clumping vaginal discharge although discharge can appear normal or be absent, with genital or vulvar itch, burning and soreness, superficial dyspareunia, external dysuria, excoriation, erythema, fissures and swelling
claims.source_text: Thick, white, clumping vaginal discharge although discharge can appear normal or be absent - Genital/vulvar itch, burning, soreness - Superficial dyspareunia - External dysuria - Excoriation, erythema, fissures, swelling

claims.claim: The majority of cases are Candida albicans, rarely other Candida species
claims.source_text: Majority Candida albicans, rarely other C andida species

claims.claim: Follow-up is not indicated for uncomplicated infection, test of cure is not required, and retesting is not indicated unless symptoms fail to resolve, when alternative diagnoses should also be considered
claims.source_text: Not indicated for uncomplicated infection. Test of Cure (TOC) Not required. Retesting Not indicated unless symptoms fail to resolve. Also consider alternative diagnoses

claims.claim: In pregnancy a longer course of topical treatment of at least 7 days may be needed, and fluconazole and boric acid are contraindicated
claims.source_text: Pregnant people May need longer course of topical treatment (e.g. 7 days minimum). Fluconazole/boric acid contraindicated
